heldBack.cp-capron: Redrew the designer's lopsided C-shaped candidate as a symmetric, tapered solid boomerang with a lighter return arrow; it is bold and fits the "threw out his own lawsuit" idea far better than the current thin, generic quill-and-inkwell outline. Scored 7 rather than 8 because at card size the boomerang-plus-arc still carries a slight "refresh icon" ambiguity. Saved to /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-danielkind-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-1dad17eb-69bf-4c4a-a7c5-9328a5b48003-688c5249-9c51-4fa9-8ad1-650000abd32e-scratch-2026-10-03-51507e/c5e31a4a-53d2-4663-863e-f8e09a2fe84b/scratchpad/brand2/out/cp-capron.txt.
heldBack.cp-shady-grove: The designer's two stacked cupped hands read as open hands at card size and point to Allstate, which is more memorable for this case than the current thin-outline knee joint; I fanned the fingertips so the finger slits survive at small size and pulled the back hand inside the 23-unit bound. It scores 7, not 8: at 34 px the fingers are still slightly feathery, and the render's DISALLOWED check was run but its output was not inspected.
heldBack.lrs-n-standing-brock: Redrawn from the designer's candidate, whose interior turned to mush at card size: now a bolder 8-tooth gear with five large heads on short bodies joined by one ring, which reads cleanly as a cog with a circle of people. It is a solid, case-specific union mark and clearly stronger than the current thin-outline shipping container, though the figures read as dots rather than people at 34 px, so I score it just under 8.
heldBack.lrs-s-weiss: Refined the designer's candidate (centred larger globe, bolder attached anchor, cleaner eagle with gaps between parts); it reads as the Marine emblem and is far more specific to this case than the generic rank chevrons. Honest caveat: at the real 34 px size it is busy and falls short of the 8 target, so the clean chevrons remain a defensible fallback if the owner prefers simplicity.
heldBack.cp-jeub: Bold solid rounded tin with the opened strip, coil and key reads as a key-wind tin at card size and is specific to the case, where the current thin fork-and-knife outline is generic and weak. I kept the designer's composition, shrinking the tin slightly and reshaping the key loop to sit inside the bounds; it scores 7 rather than 8 because a stranger may hesitate between a tin and a tape dispenser.
heldBack.lrs-s-shoemaker: The designer's candidate and my three redraws (upright, tilted, taller shaft) are bold and format-clean, but at card size an inverted boot on a post reads as a barber chair or faucet rather than a shoemaker's last. The current park bench is instantly legible and fits the Rock Creek Park caption, so it should stay.
heldBack.cp-ellis-canning: Solid block H with a taller I standing through it, separated by a clean gap, stays crisp and bold at card size where the current thin-outline burning tractor turns fussy. I thickened the designer's H and shortened the I's overshoot to match the real mark; it still relies on the viewer knowing the IH logo, hence 7 rather than 8.
